narration.text: He survived an atomic bomb. Three days later, he survived another. This is Tsutomu Yamaguchi, a Mitsubishi shipbuilding engineer. August sixth, nineteen forty-five. He was in Hiroshima on business when the United States dropped an atomic bomb. Severely burned, he survived. The next day, he boarded a train. It carried him home to Nagasaki. On August ninth, he was back at work. He recalled describing Hiroshima to his manager. Then came another flash. The second atomic bomb had struck. He survived again. His wife and infant son survived too. The bombings killed tens of thousands and left lasting suffering. In two thousand nine, Japan officially recognized his exposure in both cities. He was not the only double survivor. He lived until twenty ten, aged ninety-three. In later years, he urged the world to abolish nuclear weapons.
